entries.title: Credit Claiming: a CE claim site for each event
entries.summary: Attendees sign in to the event's claim site with their badge number or email and last name, claim CE credit for the sessions they attended, complete the session evaluation, and download one certificate per credit plus a full transcript as **PDF** or **Excel**. Organizers set it up under **Program → Configure → Settings → Claiming** and **Credit types**, and follow claims, attendance, the audit and a report by credit type under **Program → After the event → Credit Claiming**. Gatherings can offer credit too: turn on **Continuing education credit** in the gathering's **Settings**, and a guest's door check-in counts as attending every agenda item.

enable.path: Preview → Credit Claiming → Request access (event card for one conference, organization card for every event and gathering)

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming; Program → Configure → Settings → Claiming / Credit types; Gathering → Settings → Continuing education credit; Gathering → After → CE credit

entries.use_case: Accredited meetings owe every attendee a certificate and a transcript, and owe the accrediting body proof that credit went only to people who attended and evaluated the session. Credit Claiming runs that claim site on the sessions, credits and scans already in Sessionboard, so there is no separate claim vendor and no spreadsheet reconciliation after the show.

cs_action.note: Early Access Beta, two cards: feature--credit_claiming on the event (one conference) or on the org (every event and gathering; gatherings require the org flag). Independent of the org Learning (Lessons & Credits) flags; Learning stays as it is.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any medical, scientific or association meeting that awards CE/CME or nursing contact hours, or that is replacing a third-party CE claim site after the show.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers whose events award continuing-education credit and need attendees to self-claim after the event.
internal.staff_path: Event → Preview → Credit Claiming (enable for the event), then Program → Configure → Settings → Claiming
internal.gotchas: Credit types are org-wide and shared with Learning. Point General Attendance at a certificate template that does not print an amount (the built-in CE certificate reads '0 hours'). Swapcard scans need 'Pull session attendee lists & door scans' on the event mapping. The claim site and on-screen transcript show the viewer's device timezone; PDF/Excel downloads use the event timezone. Gatherings: check-in is the attendance for every agenda item; 'Who can claim' defaults to checked-in guests, and guests who never checked in are refused at sign-in. Gathering emails get a {{claim_url}} merge tag.
internal.talk_track: Set credit on your sessions, turn on the claim site, and send attendees one link. They see the sessions they scanned into first, answer the evaluation, and download certificates and a transcript; you get an audit against verified attendance and a report by credit type.

entries.title: Interest Form evaluation plans preview assignments before you apply them
entries.summary: On an Interest Form evaluation plan's **Assignments** step, **Review and apply** now previews every pairing the rule would make, by submission or by reviewer, before anything is saved, as event plans already do. **Replace not-yet-reviewed** and **Replace all** show the exact numbers to create, remove, leave in place and keep before you confirm.

where.path: Speaker CRM → Interest Forms → [form] → Evaluation → [plan] → Assignments → Review and apply

entries.use_case: Committees scoring Interest Form proposals can check who will review what, and what a Replace would remove, before anything changes — the same safety net event plans have.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why Interest Form plans showed "do not preview pairings before applying", or worries about overwriting reviewer assignments mid-cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Interest Form evaluation plans with reviewer assignments.
internal.staff_path: Speaker CRM → Interest Forms → [form] → Evaluation → [plan] → Assignments → Review and apply
internal.gotchas: Nothing is saved by the preview; assignments are written only on Assign or on confirming Replace. Counts in the Replace dialog are exact for that moment — if someone else changes assignments in between, apply reports what it actually did.
internal.talk_track: Interest Form plans now preview assignments exactly like event plans: see every reviewer–submission pairing, and the exact numbers a Replace will change, before you commit.

draft.docs_gap: The Interest Form evaluation plans guide should document the assignment preview panel under the "Review and apply" step, including what the create/remove/keep counts mean and how the Replace confirmation works.
draft.why_use_it: Interest Form evaluation plans let you score and assign reviewers to submissions collected outside a specific event. The preview panel gives you a dry-run view of assignment changes so you can confirm the impact before any records are written, matching the safety controls already available in session-based evaluation plans.

entries.title: SSO self-service setup: share a guided link so your IT team configures SAML or OIDC directly
entries.summary: Staff can create a SAML or OIDC identity-provider shell with just a name and domain, then share a secure **Setup Link** with the customer's IT team. The IT team opens a dedicated **Enterprise SSO Setup** page to enter connection details, map claims, add IT contacts, run a live sign-in test, and track wizard progress — all without needing a Sessionboard login. A config moves through **Pending → Configured → Verified** states; enforcing SSO now requires a **Verified** config. Once verified, the setup form becomes read-only via the shared link, and staff editing remains unrestricted.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable SSO; then Organization Settings → Security → Single Sign-On

where.path: Organization Settings → Security → Single Sign-On → Setup Link

entries.use_case: Organizers who need their IT department to configure SSO can hand off the technical setup without granting Sessionboard admin access. The IT team follows a step-by-step wizard, runs a real sign-in test against their identity provider, and confirms completion — all through a time-limited, token-authenticated link.

cs_action.note: The UI counterpart (sessionboard-web-ui-v2 branch feature/SB-8293) must be merged and deployed after this API PR. Also verify that the v1 SSO relay allow-list includes the APPV2_URL origin in every region (US, EU, ME) before sharing the first setup link with a customer — missing origin causes the sign-in test to strand on the v1 error page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or customer says their IT team needs to configure SSO but doesn't have (or shouldn't have) Sessionboard admin access, or when SSO setup has stalled because of back-and-forth on connection fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise customers and any org using or evaluating SSO (SAML or OIDC) where the Sessionboard admin and the IT/IdP owner are different people.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Security → Single Sign-On → create a config in setup mode → Generate Setup Link
internal.gotchas: Existing enforced SSO configs on main are backfilled to Verified by the migration, so no customer is blocked on upgrade. The setup link expires after 24 hours once the config is verified (read-only after that via the public link; staff editing is always available). The development-only flag SSO_SETUP_ALLOW_LOCAL_IDP must never be set in production. No email notifications for IT contacts are sent yet — that is a follow-up ticket.
internal.talk_track: You can now create an SSO config shell and send your IT team a secure, time-limited link to a guided setup wizard. They enter the connection details, map claims, add their contact info, and run a live sign-in test — all without a Sessionboard login. Once they verify it works, the config is locked in and you can enforce SSO with one click.

draft.docs_gap: The SSO guide should document the new self-service setup flow: creating a shell config in setup mode, generating and sharing a Setup Link, the Pending → Configured → Verified lifecycle, the IT contacts feature, the live sign-in test, wizard progress tracking, and the requirement that enforcing SSO now requires a Verified config.
draft.why_use_it: SSO lets your attendees, speakers, and team members sign in to Sessionboard using your organization's existing identity provider, eliminating separate passwords and centralizing access control. The self-service setup link means your IT team can configure and verify the connection on their own schedule without waiting for a Sessionboard admin to relay every field value. A built-in sign-in test confirms the integration works before you enforce it, and the Pending → Configured → Verified lifecycle prevents an incomplete config from being enforced by mistake.

entries.title: Enterprise SSO self-service setup: shareable setup link and guided wizard for IT teams
entries.summary: Organizers can now set up SAML and OIDC identity providers end-to-end without leaving Sessionboard. The **Add identity provider** dialog asks for Name, Domain, and Protocol; after creation the IdP's edit sidebar opens showing a **Share setup link** card (generate, copy, regenerate, revoke) alongside the manual connection form. A customer's IT team opens the link at `/enterprise-sso-setup/<token>` and walks through a five-step wizard — **Identity provider → Create the application → Identity provider details → Map your user attributes → Test sign-in** — with progress saved on every step. Staff see a compact status badge (**Not configured / Configured — not tested / Verified / Waiting for customer**) next to each IdP in the **Enterprise SSO** list, and **Enforce login** becomes available only after a verified test. An **IT contacts** section on the wizard and in the edit sidebars lets staff record up to five contacts per IdP.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable SSO; then Organization Settings → Enterprise SSO

entries.use_case: Event teams that rely on corporate SSO can hand off the technical configuration to their IT department via a secure, time-limited setup link — no admin credentials required. Staff retain full visibility into setup progress and can complete the connection manually at any time if preferred.

cs_action.note: The API PR (sessionboard-web-api#4713) must be deployed in all regions before this UI is usable. Machine translations for de/es/fr strings need native review before non-English customers see them. Twelve manual browser QA cases (staff M1–M6, customer M7–M12) were not run in the automated suite and should be verified in a staging environment before customer rollout.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a prospect or customer asks about SSO setup complexity, IT team involvement, or reducing time-to-go-live for identity provider configuration.
internal.who_should_get_it: Enterprise customers with SAML or OIDC identity providers who want their IT team to handle the technical SSO configuration without needing Sessionboard admin access.
internal.staff_path: Organization Settings → Enterprise SSO → Add identity provider → (after creation) Share setup link
internal.gotchas: The public setup page at /enterprise-sso-setup/<token> is only functional after the companion API PR #4713 is live in every region. A verified connection opened via a setup link is read-only in the wizard (forms disabled with a notice); the sign-in test and IT contacts remain available. Enforce login is gated on a verified test — a 409 is rendered inline if attempted before verification. The setup link token travels only in the Authorization header and sessionStorage, never in the URL.
internal.talk_track: Instead of emailing configuration instructions back and forth with a customer's IT team, you generate a secure setup link from the Enterprise SSO settings page. The IT team opens it, follows a five-step wizard to configure their identity provider, runs a test sign-in, and you see the status update to Verified in real time. Once verified, you can enforce SSO login with one click.

draft.docs_gap: The SSO guide should be updated to document the new self-service setup flow: the Add identity provider dialog (name/domain/protocol only), the Share setup link card in the edit sidebar, the five-step public wizard at /enterprise-sso-setup/<token>, the IT contacts section, the status badges (Not configured / Configured — not tested / Verified / Waiting for customer), progress persistence, the sign-in test polling flow, and the rename of the settings menu entry to "Enterprise SSO".
draft.why_use_it: Single Sign-On lets your attendees and team members authenticate with your organization's existing identity provider instead of managing separate Sessionboard passwords. The self-service setup flow gives your IT team a guided, five-step wizard — covering application creation, metadata exchange, attribute mapping, and a live sign-in test — so configuration happens without back-and-forth with Sessionboard support. Staff control when to share the link, can track progress in real time, and can enforce SSO login only after a successful test, reducing the risk of locking anyone out.

entries.title: Expand Contacts, Groups or Sessions rows to see up to three kinds of related records inline
entries.summary: A **Related** button at the end of the table toolbar lets you add up to three related record types to a Contacts, Groups or Sessions table, such as a session's participants and groups, or a contact's sessions. Each type starts with sensible default columns that you can switch on or off and drag to reorder, and has its own sort and filter that work like the table's own **Sort** and **Filter** tabs. Rows with related records show a chevron and count; expanding one opens a nested table with its own pagination and inline editing. Related settings count as Saved View changes and save with the view. Export can include the nested rows: XLSX grouped under each parent, or CSV with one row per parent and related record.

enable.path: Not yet available to customers: Sessionboard staff only while in limited release

where.path: Event → Contacts / Groups / Sessions → table toolbar → Related

entries.use_case: Show teams that need submission, submitter, and speaker details in one view can expand any row to see related records without building a separate custom report. Teams managing sponsors or exhibitors can expand a group row to see all associated contacts and their session participation without leaving the table.

cs_action.note: Staff-only (super user) while in limited release; customers cannot see the Related button yet. Use it to demo, not to promise a date.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks for a combined view of submissions + submitters + speakers, or when a show team is building custom reports just to see related records side by side.
internal.who_should_get_it: Show teams (e.g. Tahaluf) that build custom reports just to see submission, submitter and speaker details side by side.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts / Groups / Sessions → table toolbar → Related (super users only)
internal.gotchas: One level deep only. Not on the org CRM, Agenda list or org Sessions directories. Nested rows and counts follow the viewer's session and contact scope, so restricted team members see only records they could open themselves. Nested XLSX does not split datetime columns the way parent rows do.
internal.talk_track: Instead of building a custom report every time you need to see a contact's sessions or a sponsor's contacts, you can now expand any row in the Contacts, Groups, or Sessions table to see related records inline — with editable cells, filters, and export support.

entries.title: Restrict a team member to the contacts that match rules you set
entries.summary: A **Contact access** section on a restricted team member lets you limit which contacts they can see. Build rules on standard fields (such as name, email, company or contact type) and custom fields with **is**, **is not**, **contains** and **is empty**, match **all** or **any** of them, or pick a static contact list. Contacts outside the scope are hidden from the contacts list, search, pickers, exports and profile links. On sessions, the agenda and session exports, out-of-scope participants appear as **Restricted** rows. Emails they send skip out-of-scope recipients, and Insights queries return only in-scope rows.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager: Sessionboard staff set Contact access on the team member for you while it is in limited release

where.path: Event → Team → (member) → Edit → Restrict records → Contact access

entries.use_case: Hosting and travel vendors who should only see the speakers they are responsible for can be given a restricted role scoped to a "Hosted = Yes" checkbox field, so they never see other speakers' names, emails, or headshots — even when those speakers share a session.

cs_action.note: Built for Tahaluf's hosting / travel vendors. Staff (super users) configure Contact access on the customer's team member; the restriction then applies to that member everywhere.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to give a vendor access to only certain speakers, or when they report that session-scoped roles expose too many contacts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with multi-vendor events (e.g. Tahaluf-style hosted speaker programmes) where different vendors manage different subsets of speakers.
internal.staff_path: Event → Team → (member) → Edit → Restrict records → Contact access (super users only)
internal.gotchas: Session filters and contact rules AND together. Static lists only, not dynamic segments. Unreadable rules fail closed (the member sees no contacts). Roster merge tags in emails still list every speaker on the session, by design. Not yet scope-aware: Insights dashboard computed counts and the automated-email forecast count. Admin roles are never restricted.
internal.talk_track: You can now give a hosting vendor a role that shows only the speakers they are responsible for — set a 'Hosted' checkbox on each speaker, then point the vendor's role at 'Hosted = Yes' in Contact access. They see those contacts everywhere in the event: list, search, export, email campaigns, and session profiles. Anyone outside that scope is hidden or shown as Restricted.

entries.title: Add contacts to a session in bulk from the CRM, across any event, with an acceptance status
entries.summary: **Add to session** in the CRM now works for contacts who are not in any event yet, and lists every org event you can manage (not just the contact's own events). Adding someone to a session in a new event adds them to that event first. A new **Add to session** bulk action on the org Contacts table and on the event Contacts table places up to 200 selected contacts on one session at once, with one role, and reports anyone who could not be added. When the event has speaker acceptance turned on, a **Status** picker (**Pending** / **Accepted**) sets the participant status in the same step. Events that do not use Sessions 2.0 show a message instead of adding.

where.path: Org CRM → Contacts → contact profile → Submissions card → Add to session; Org CRM → Contacts → select contacts → Add to session; Event → Contacts → select contacts → Add to session

entries.use_case: Teams that confirm speakers before the agenda is finalised can now assign a contact to a session — and set them as Accepted — directly from the CRM without first adding them to an event manually. Bulk assignment lets programme teams place a whole panel or track cohort onto a session in one action instead of editing each contact individually.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says adding speakers to sessions from the CRM is tedious, or when they keep placeholder sessions because speakers are confirmed before the agenda exists.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the CRM who manages speakers across multiple events or confirms speakers before sessions are scheduled — especially large conference teams like Tahaluf/Informa.
internal.staff_path: Org CRM → Contacts → contact profile → Submissions card → Add to session; or the Add to session button in either Contacts table's bulk bar
internal.gotchas: Bulk is capped at 200 contacts; selecting more shows a toast and posts nothing. The Status picker only appears when the event has speaker acceptance on; otherwise the participant is saved as pending. Events not on Sessions 2.0 block Add (single and bulk) with a message; add those contacts from the session itself. The event Contacts bulk button is hidden in sponsor and exhibitor modes and needs session update permission.
internal.talk_track: You can add any contact to a session straight from the CRM, even before they are in the event, and mark them Accepted in the same step. Select up to 200 contacts and put them all on one session, or create the session on the spot.

entries.title: Evaluator and Assignment imports accept several submission IDs per row, and sub-session IDs
entries.summary: The **Submission ID** column of the **Import Evaluators** and **Import Assignments** spreadsheets now takes several IDs in one cell, separated by commas, semicolons or pipes, so one row can assign an evaluator to many submissions. Sub-session IDs such as `SESS-1977-2` now work too. A wrong or unknown ID skips that row with an error naming the ID, instead of failing with a database error.

where.path: Evaluation Plans → Plan → Plan Options → Import Evaluators / Import Assignments

entries.use_case: An admin can assign one evaluator to a whole stack of submissions from a single spreadsheet row, and can target sub-sessions (common for abstracts) by the ID they see in the grid, instead of getting an error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to assign one reviewer to many submissions by import, or reports that the evaluator or assignment import fails on a list of IDs or on a sub-session ID like SESS-1977-2.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone using Evaluation Plan 2.0 imports, especially programs that review sub-sessions or abstracts.
internal.staff_path: Evaluation Plans → Plan → Plan Options → Import Evaluators / Import Assignments
internal.gotchas: A cell with commas must be quoted in a CSV; Excel and Google Sheets do this automatically when saving, hand-written CSVs may not. One bad ID skips the whole row. Lists of more than about six UUIDs may hit the CSVBox widget's own column limit if its dashboard sheet still sets 255 characters; friendly IDs (SESS-123) fit easily. One-submission-per-row files work exactly as before.
internal.talk_track: Put the submission IDs in one cell separated by commas, like SESS-101, SESS-102, SESS-123-2, and that evaluator gets all of them. Sub-session IDs work as shown in the grid. If one ID is wrong, that row is skipped and the error tells you which ID to fix.

draft.docs_gap: The guide's "Import assignments from a spreadsheet" section should be updated to document that Submission ID accepts a comma-, semicolon-, pipe-, or newline-separated list of IDs and that sub-session IDs (e.g. SESS-123-2) are supported.
draft.why_use_it: The Evaluators and Assignments imports let you set up your entire review programme from a spreadsheet in one step. You can assign evaluators to specific submissions, map them to rounds, and undo a run if something goes wrong — all without touching each record by hand. This is especially useful when you have hundreds of reviewers and thousands of submissions to wire together before a review cycle opens.

entries.title: Swapcard: map a Sessionboard field to "Make the session private" and stop syncs from resetting it
entries.summary: A new destination field **Make the session private** is available in the Swapcard field-mapping UI. Map a checkbox, dropdown, or text field from Sessionboard to control whether each session is private in Swapcard. When no mapping is set, syncs now preserve whatever privacy value Swapcard already holds instead of resetting every session to public.

where.path: Org Settings → Integrations → Swapcard → Field mappings → Session fields → Make the session private

entries.use_case: Organizers who mark certain sessions as private in Swapcard (e.g. invite-only or internal sessions) no longer need to re-apply that setting after every sync. They can also drive the private flag directly from a Sessionboard field so the setting is managed in one place.

cs_action.note: The bug affected all 94 production Swapcard mappings (85 US, 9 EU). Any customer who had manually re-privatised sessions in Swapcard after each sync will now find those sessions stay private automatically. Confirm with affected accounts (especially Informa Connect/Tech — AI Summit NY, World AI Cannes) that the new behaviour matches expectations before their next scheduled sync.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Swapcard reports that private sessions keep becoming public after a sync, or asks how to control session visibility from Sessionboard.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers with active Swapcard mappings, particularly those running large events with private or invite-only sessions.
internal.staff_path: Org Settings → Integrations → Swapcard → Field mappings → Session fields
internal.gotchas: If nothing is mapped, the sync sends back the privacy value Swapcard already holds, so sessions that earlier syncs made public stay public until someone fixes them in Swapcard Studio or maps a field. Only checkbox, dropdown and text fields can be mapped; saving any other type, or two fields, is refused with an error. An empty or unrecognized dropdown/text value leaves the Swapcard setting unchanged.
internal.talk_track: Every Swapcard sync used to silently reset all sessions to public — this fix stops that. You can also now map any checkbox, dropdown, or text field in Sessionboard to drive the private flag in Swapcard, so your access rules are managed in one place.

draft.why_use_it: The Swapcard integration lets you push your program — sessions, speakers, and their details — from Sessionboard into Swapcard without manual re-entry. Mapping fields gives you a single source of truth: change a value in Sessionboard and the next sync carries it across. Controlling session privacy through the mapping means your access rules in Swapcard stay consistent with your program data rather than requiring a separate manual step after each sync.
